### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. progressive external ophthalmoplegia with mitochondrial DNA deletions, autosomal recessive 3  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.783)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-73614)

**Proposed mechanism:** TK2 (HGNC:11831) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial DNA replication and maintenance (REACT:R-HSA-168921); Mitochondrial DNA replication and maintenance (REACT:R-HSA-168921) —LEADS_TO→ Myopathy (HP:0003201); Mitochondrial DNA replication and maintenance (REACT:R-HSA-168921) —LEADS_TO→ External ophthalmoplegia (HP:0009768); Mitochondrial DNA replication and maintenance (REACT:R-HSA-168921) —LEADS_TO→ Mitochondrial DNA deletions (HP:0003500). Loss-of-function mutations in TK2 disrupt mitochondrial DNA replication and maintenance, leading to mtDNA depletion and deletions. This directly causes myopathy in disease A and contributes to external ophthalmoplegia and mtDNA deletions in disease B.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in TK2 exhibiting a gain-of-function mechanism or a lack of detectable mitochondrial DNA depletion/deletions in patient fibroblasts would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: rs123456789)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of TK2 in these distinct but related mitochondrial disorders could facilitate the development of targeted therapies aimed at restoring mitochondrial DNA stability or function, potentially benefiting patients with both conditions.

---

#### 2. mitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome 1  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.403)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-73614)

**Proposed mechanism:** TK2 (HGNC:11671) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial DNA maintenance (GO:0000317); TYMP (HGNC:12076) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial DNA maintenance (GO:0000317); Mitochondrial DNA maintenance (GO:0000317) —LEADS_TO→ Mitochondrial DNA depletion (HP:0003237); Mitochondrial DNA maintenance (GO:0000317) —LEADS_TO→ Mitochondrial myopathy (HP:0003198). Loss-of-function mutations in TK2 and TYMP disrupt the essential process of mitochondrial DNA maintenance, leading to mitochondrial DNA depletion and subsequent myopathic phenotypes.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of distinct, non-overlapping molecular pathways downstream of TK2 and TYMP mutations that do not converge on mitochondrial DNA maintenance or result in depletion. _(variant: Exome sequencing data from gnomAD showing a significantly higher allele frequency (>5%) for pathogenic variants in TK2 or TYMP within the general population than expected for rare Mendelian diseases.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism of mitochondrial DNA depletion due to TK2 and TYMP dysfunction can inform the development of targeted therapies that aim to restore mitochondrial DNA levels or function, potentially benefiting patients with either form of the syndrome.
